summary.intent: Open a draft PR (#2145) for the cold-start file-rows listing fix in CipherBox, run multi-lane reviews (simplify, security, crypto-privacy, code review), and fold the findings into the PR.
summary.outcome: The draft PR was opened and four review gates reported. The fold lane removed the inline boundary walk and replaced it with a latch, added one shared per-scope leg builder, and moved the root mapping to the WASM host. All engine, wasm, fuse and web suites and the 30/30 smoke slice pass, but nothing is committed yet.

repo: The engine's `boundary_walk_ran` flag was set at walk start, so a navigation during an in-flight or failed walk read a shared folder under the vault root seed. The adoption gate then rejected the rows and emitted a false AttributableAbuse. The fix is a `boundary_walk_landed` latch, set only on `Ok` after the boundary sets are installed. `refresh_focus_on_access` queues the folder's children and returns before any read leg until the latch is set.

The desktop FUSE host never sends SetFocus, so `open_folder` is always None there. An engine-level 'root in view' fallback would make every tick resolve root rows, which conflicts with blueprint/desktop.md's refresh-on-access rule. Mapping a null focus to the root at the WASM host (`focus_names_the_root`) avoids this.

In `snapshotStore.ts` the focus now starts as `undefined`, so the first `setFocus(null)` is sent. `useFolderNavigation.test.tsx` now expects `[null, DOCS]` because the mount sends the root focus first.

The tick and the facade navigation duplicated the per-scope leg setup (unproved skip, seed, floors, scope root name, own-vs-grafted plane), and the two copies had already drifted. They now share `ScopeLegContext::material` in `sync/pass.rs`.
Web-e2e fixtures: the `device` fixture lives in `tests/web-e2e/devices.ts` as `deviceTest` and `OpenDevice`. Putting it in `fixtures.ts` would create an import cycle (devices → vault → fixtures).
Each Rust integration test file builds as its own crate, so sharing helpers such as `recipient_identity` and `import_recipient` needs a shared module via `#[path]`, as `content_wipe.rs` does.
A web-e2e spec with no tag runs in the Web E2E Smoke slice, because smoke uses `grepInvert: /@full/`.
Type-erased holders such as `Sweeper` exist because the command path lacks the `Clone + 'static` bounds. `BoundaryWalk` was modelled on it but was deleted in the fold.

code.finding: `walk_scopes` set `boundary_walk_ran` as its first line, before any await. It was therefore true while the walk was in flight, failed, or never started. The fix sets `boundary_walk_landed` only on `Ok` after the install.

`navigation_file_legs` copied the tick's per-scope leg from `pass.rs:616-678`. It decided `is_own_scope` from the proved set but took floors from `scope_floors`, which also counts minted scopes. It also re-read `root` after an await, which broke the 'one root read' comment.
`clear_failed_start` clears only the spawner, not `boundary_walk`, so a failed start keeps `TickPass` and its seams alive. This became moot once `BoundaryWalk` was deleted.
A test comment said the web host sends the forced refresh before the focus. The same PR reverses that order in `snapshotStore.ts`, so the comment was false.

workflow: Run several independent review lanes (simplify, security, crypto-privacy, code review) over the same diff. Two or more lanes independently confirmed the main flaw, the flag-timing race, so the overlap is a useful confidence signal.

After the review reports landed, a follow-up redirect to the in-flight fold agent via SendMessage replaced one planned fix with a better one: map the root at the WASM host instead of adding an engine rule.
Check that tests catch the bug by deliberately breaking the fix. Here that meant setting the latch at walk start and removing the gate, and the failed-walk test caught both.
`git checkout main -- <file>` restores single files without switching branches.
Keep an invariant's comment at one home and link to it elsewhere, per AGENTS.md. Several review findings flagged the same reason stated three times.

friction: The first-draft inline boundary walk reintroduced the race it was meant to fix, and also made the first navigation wait on a network round trip, so offline cold starts wait out the adopt timeout. It took four review lanes to expose this.
Several test comments and docs went stale within the same PR, such as the web-host command-order narration and the 'one root read' comment.
The fold agent ran about 13 minutes and had to be redirected mid-flight when the code review showed the desktop conflict.
Six tests that navigated before any tick needed an extra tick in the shared fixture after the latch change.
open_items: Commit and push the fold, which is currently uncommitted. After that, re-check CI on the new push; the first push had 34 checks green and one still running.
An `Ok` walk with `failure` set still sets the latch. This follows the 'on Ok' rule and matches what the tick reads, but it may deserve revisiting.
The two cold-start e2e tests each seed an identical NESTED vault. Sharing the seed was rejected for isolation, so revisit it only if suite time becomes a problem.
The first navigation still duplicates the first tick's floors, adopt and walk once per session. This was accepted as a one-time cost.
A security-review note on desktop root rows crowding the 64-slot focus queue was addressed by removing the engine root rule. Verify that no desktop path still pays for it.
The `smoke` description in blueprint/testing.md (line ~258) may need an update, since the spec adds three two-device tests.
`walk_boundaries` was deleted, so the earlier note about `consult_scope_pointers` being skipped no longer applies. Confirm the tick path still behaves as on main.
